translation_notes: same shape as isamplesorg/vocabularies' VocabularyStore.narrower/broader (sibling regions in this stratum): the query text never concatenates a TERM (`v`/`r` already travel via `initBindings`); what is assembled by `+` is the PROLOGUE (`PFX + """SELECT ..."""`). `?parent` (here spelled `r`) is not projected (only `?s` is in SELECT), so it becomes a direct term interpolation instead of a bindings-call; the module-level `PFX` string (rdf:/rdfs:/owl:/skos:) collapses to a single `@prefix skos:` since only skos: is used by these queries.

TRANSPILER DEFECT, confirmed and worth reporting as-is (ldpy/012-style constat, not a limitation of the language design): `s{ ... {r} ... }` -- a bare single-character interpolation whose expression text is exactly `r` -- crashes the transpiler with `IndexError: string index out of range` in `_string_end` (core.py), because the sub-scan that validates the interpolation as a Python expression mistakes the identifier `r` for the start of a raw-string literal (`r'...'`/`r"..."`) and then finds no closing quote. Reproduced in isolation with a 6-line minimal file (`s{ SELECT ?s WHERE { ?s skos:broader {r} . } }`). Any expression starting with `r`/`R`/`b`/`B`/`f`/`F`/`u`/`U` (Python's string-prefix letters) immediately inside `{` is a suspect of the same class; only the bare single-letter case was verified here.

workaround used (not a refactoring of the ORIGINAL program, only of how the SPARQL interpolation is spelled): `{(r)}` instead of `{r}` -- parenthesising defeats the prefix-letter misparse while remaining the exact same Python expression. Both branches of the region use it, since both interpolate the bare parameter `r`.

classified minor-restructuring rather than directly-expressible for the same reason as the sibling regions: recognising the unprojected variable and retiring the `PFX +` string concatenation in favour of `@prefix` is a structural choice, on top of which the parenthesising workaround above was needed purely to route around the transpiler defect.

repair.driver: seven calls with rdflib.URIRef for r and v, the type the repository passes (r comes from query rows, tools/vocab2md.py:178-189, 242, 256, 309): several solutions in each branch, each scheme deciding (VocabA, VocabB, absent VocabC), the broader term deciding inside the v branch (Plant), zero solutions in each branch (Rock); fixture neighbours Horse (skos:topConceptOf instead of skos:inScheme), Lynx (in both schemes, must come back once), Fish now in VocabA. The three str calls are kept.
repair.remaining: SELECT DISTINCT in the v branch is an equivalent mutant (every term but ?s is bound, no duplicate possible): not counted. The three original str calls still return [] on both sides; the repository never passes a str, nor r=None (None would leave ?parent unbound in the original and become Literal('None') in the translation, known gap 9) -- not exercised, by design.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: prepareQuery disappears (`g.query(PFX + "...", initBindings=...)`), the result loop becomes `[row[0] for row in qres]`, and each query fits on one line. The SPARQL text keeps its tokens, on both sides.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g` and two s{ }, with the same comprehension. The `{(r)}` workaround stays: `s{ ... {r} ... }` still crashes the transpiler (IndexError in _string_end, checked again on this ldpy version). No exception to the symmetry.
The notation gains nothing here (ratio 1.0): the Python query strings count one token each, while the island bodies are counted as RDF.
